## Description

Summary tables are central to nearly every research report, from the
"Table 1" describing a study population to detailed tables of outcomes
and adverse events. Yet producing them reproducibly, and consistently
across projects, often means writing custom formatting code again and
again. {gtsummary} is the most widely used R package for creating
presentation-ready summary tables, offering sensible defaults alongside
a high degree of customization.

This seminar introduces {gtsummary} for researchers and analysts who are
comfortable in R but new to the package. We begin with `tbl_summary()`,
showing how a single function call produces a publication-ready table
and how add-on functions append overall columns, p-values, and
(optionally adjusted) group differences. We then extend these ideas to
hierarchical tables, such as adverse event summaries, and show how
complex tables can be assembled from simple parts by merging and
stacking.

Next, we look under the hood: every number in a {gtsummary} table is
stored as an Analysis Results Dataset (ARD), a machine-readable record
that makes results traceable and reusable, and tables can be built
directly from ARDs as well. We also cover print engines for rendering
tables to different output formats, and themes that apply a journal's
style or a group's house standards to every table at once.

Finally, we discuss how these standards can be written down for AI
coding agents, so that an agent produces tables that follow them
without constant reminders. Attendees will leave knowing how to get
started with {gtsummary} and where to go next to tailor it to their own
work.

![](images/dan-circle.png){fig-alt="Headshot of Daniel Sjoberg"}

[**Daniel D. Sjoberg**](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/){.instructor-name}

[Executive Director of Data Science & Clinical Data Analytics, Kardigan (he/him)]{.instructor-role}

Daniel leads the Data Science and Clinical Analytics groups at Kardigan. Previously was a Senior Principal Innovation Data Scientist and Real-time Analytics Group Lead at Genentech, a Lead Data Science Manager at the Prostate Cancer Clinical Trials Consortium, and an academic biostatistician at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center for 13 years. He enjoys R package development, creating many packages on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/), [R-Universe](https://ddsjoberg.r-universe.dev/ui#packages), and [GitHub](https://github.com/ddsjoberg). He's a co-organizer of [rainbowR](https://rainbowr.netlify.app/) and of the [R Medicine Conference](https://rconsortium.github.io/RMedicine_website/), and a recipient of the Brian Bole Award for Excellence from Open Source in Pharma and the ASA Innovation in Programming Award.
